text: {"standards":[{"code":"SL.6.1","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Seminar or Podcast Rounds have students hold small-group discussions where they build on peers' ideas, and the Paraphrase Before You Respond activity practices responding to a partner."},{"code":"SL.6.2","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the What We Learned think-pair-share, students explain how a classmate's visual or sound helped them understand a lesson from The Lightning Thief."},{"code":"SL.6.4","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Prepare Your Presentation and Seminar or Podcast Rounds, students deliver a two-minute claim-evidence-value talk in a logical order, with rehearsed eye contact, volume, and pronunciation."},{"code":"SL.6.5","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Prepare Your Presentation, students choose and add a visual or audio element to clarify their point, and then use it during the Seminar or Podcast Rounds."},{"code":"SL.6.6","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Say It Clearly activity and the ELD formal-versus-casual model have students adapt their speech to a formal presentation and use formal, complete sentences."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"uses","reason":"The Prepare Your Presentation activity names The Lightning Thief as a text, and students cite its evidence and characters (Percy, Medusa, the Underworld) throughout the talks and seminar."}}
